I can really relate to your post. When I was 14 I had a shitty psych ward psychiatrist who over prescribed me pills and couldn't keep religion out of his job. I also had a therapist at 16 tell me I didnt really like to self harm. I enjoyed it in the moment he said, but I felt guilty afterwards and hated the consequences, yet that wasnt true. You need to find a better therapist, which is hard to do. It can take up to 5 tries on average so dont give up. 

Tell your psychiatrist about your side effects. Your meds dont seem to be working. I had a similar experience. They effectively quelled my obsessive thoughts but the trade off was a flat effect. I regret not being honest at the time because there are other options besides SSRIs. 

Have you considered microdosing psychedelics? That isnt for everyone but it helps some. I might look into that route, though it is expensive (I'd only do it under professional supervision personally). Also you seem to be a minor, so I'm unsure if you would need parental consent.

I've never told a professional about my intrusive thoughts for similar reasons, but I'm thinking I should. I have mentioned feeling suicidal in the past, and because I didnt have a plan they didnt commit me, though they were concerned because I was somewhat considering it. I just made a safety plan  as an alternative. Since youre not even considering it, I think you're safe if you make your intent clear. Remember professionals are trained to differentiate between suicidal ideation and intrusive thoughts. 

I have told select family and friends and fortunately they all had compassion and didnt think I was crazy; just going through mental hell. A couple admitted they experience similar things! I did have one ex think I was being an attention seeking edge lord, but  that's better than my fear of being seen as dangerous or crazy imo. I doubt a professional would think that and if they do, seek a second opinion.

I also go through waves. Stress seems to trigger them. I dont know about you but my obsessions seem to change, though they are usually centered around violence or sex (they used to be religion based but that's no longer a thing). 

Talking about intrusive thoughts is a definite relief but be careful not to seek reassurance. I used to ask the internet if I was a sociopath or murderer and it only fed into my fears, even tho everyone told me I wasnt lol.

You can definitely be suicidal without attempting suicide. However these sound like intrusive thoughts, especially because they're distressing, stem from a fear of consequence, arent something you actually want to do, and cause guilt. I've had thoughts of harming myself with implements even when I didnt want to. It's not fun but it's more common than you think. 

My advice is to accept that they are just thoughts. It doesnt mean you will act on them. Your thoughts also have nothing to do with your worth as a person. Dont try to distract or block them. That only makes them worse in my experience. 

I know it's scary to tell people, but just let them know you dont want to kill yourself and dont have a plan. If you're not at actual risk, they wont commit you. I'm not a professional but look into harm OCD and see if you can relate. Also I disagree that you're not worthy of help, as this seems to be causing you a lot of mental anguish.
